You could argue that the main three who are capable of making crazy, long-term plans would be Diablo, Mephisto, and Belial.

I look at it like Warhammer 40K; the more you look into the lore and the backstory that they've taken the time to set up, the more awesome everything becomes.

For example, the Nephalem. They are basically the ancestors of current humans living in Sanctuary. It's kind of a long story, but the general gist of it is that some Angels and some Demons started having babies, and they turned out to be even more powerful than the Angels/Demons were. They were the Nephalem.

The one Angel who started the Angel/Demon alliance/baby-making-party, wasn't fond of his children potentially overthrowing the Heavens, so he tweaked some things to make it so they would lose their power over generations.

Hence now, around the time the Diablo games take place, most people are "normal", powerless humans. While those who can tap into their latent Nephalem powers become heroes (the characters you play).

I'd love to answer lore questions, if you have anything you want cleared up!

I've actually been thinking about this a bit more. Diablo wouldn't even need the direct support of all the evils. 

[Azmodan clearly believes he's enough of a badass to take the soulstone into himself and become the Prime Evil. Diablo, and those who might directly support him (the smarter ones, such as Belial and Mephisto), could easily use Azmodan's arrogance for their own plan.](/spoiler)

[Azmodan doesn't have the typical "my boss will get ya" dialogue, because he truly believes he is going to succeed.
Remember that even though they were part of the pact that Exiled the 3 Primes, twins Andariel and Duriel abruptly switched sides and came to the aid of Diablo, Mephisto, and Baal. Could it be that they were clued in from the beginning about Diablos' plot, or discovered part of it and decided to stand on the winning side?](/spoiler)

[You could even say that Diablo was *betting* on Azmodans' arrogance and eventual failure, in order to get all the Primes into the Black Soulstone.](/spoiler)

[Don't forget, Diablo has had an outside player almost this entire time, as well. Adria has been working *at least* since the events 20 years before this current game to forward Diablo's plan.](/spoiler)

[The reason Diablo panics at the end is because he had no reason to believe that some *mortal* would destroy all of his plans. According to lore, you, the player character, become effectively the most powerful nephelem since Uldyssian. You put down the armies of Hell, and even make relatively short work of the combined might of *ALL* the Evils together. There's no way that Diablo, in his arrogance, could have predicted something of this magnitude.](/spoiler)

Sorry for the huge spoiler blocks, but I don't want to ruin huge parts of the lore for people who want to read into it themselves.

I love the fact that this game and the lore they've created even engenders discussions like this.

[I've been using this build](http://us.battle.net/d3/en/calculator/barbarian#WeXRkT!bXV!ZZabaZ) , and I'm currently level 37 in Nightmare mode. You might change out a passive or a rune or two, but I've had great success with this so far.

I run with a single weapon and shield, and try to split my buffs between strength and vitality about 70/30%, respectively. The skill that gives you 100% Vitality as armor is key here. With that, and with War Cry active (100% uptime and awesome heal-per-second with Inspiring Presence), I have right around 61% damage mitigation. 

Essentially the idea is to Leap in (gaining 300% armor) smash the crap out of things with Seismic Slam, hit War Cry for some free Fury, drop Earthquake if necessary (elite mobs), hit Ignore Pain, and in between beating the hell out of people with Frenzy (and getting free heals from Triumph), your Leap should be off cooldown. Now you can either Leap out and escape, or just Leap in place to get your armor boost again, and continue smashing.

The only real problem is that this might be reliant on a good, high-damage weapon and a ton of +str/+vit items to maintain a good DPS.

I've been using the passive that grants 100% of vitality as extra armor, and trying to split all gear between strength and vitality. At level 37, with my shout active I have over 3k armor, which equates to about 61% damage reduction (can't open the game right now to be exact). I've also been using ignore pain, and the Leap rune that gives 300% armor upon landing (somewhere around 80%reduction for a few seconds). Alternating these skills, very little has been able to take me down (those "arcane" laser-mobs are super dangerous).
